items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The names say what they do (buildWindowClause, windowSum, preceding/following). Each .window() method has a JSDoc block, the error messages are clear, and formatting matches the surrounding dialect code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: buildWindowClause is shared across dialects, but the name-validation block (`if (!name || name.length === 0) throw ... non-empty`) is copy-pasted into five select.ts files. The windows type literal is also repeated in five select.types.ts files. window.ts is likely over 500 lines (windowCount is at L528).

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are validated where they enter the API: ntile/nthValue reject non-positive integers, preceding/following reject negatives and non-integers, rows/range check from/to order, and .window() rejects empty and whitespace-only names. Positional numbers are emitted as raw SQL, never bound params. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The change is purely additive. Each of the five *SelectConfig types gets an optional `windows?` field, and pg/mysql/sqlite/gel/singlestore all get the same .window(). windowSql is undefined when no windows are set, so existing SQL is unchanged. All 566 P2P tests pass.
